newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CARDINALS ACQUIRE SLUGGER MARK MCGWIRE FROM A'S.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARDINALS ACQUIRE SLUGGER MARK MCGWIRE FROM A'S.

text.p: The St Louis Cardinals picked up one of baseball's greatest home run hitters ahead of the midnight trading deadine Thursday, acquiring Mark McGwire from Oakland for three pitchers.
The 33-year-old nine-time All-Star will be reunited with Cardinals manager Tony La Russa, who managed him for 10 years with the Athletics.
"If I have a chance to go help someone get to the playoffs and the World Series, I want that opportunity," said McGwire, whose 34 home runs is second in the American League this season.
St Louis sent right-hander T.J. Mathews and minor-leaguers Eric Ludwick and Blake Stein to Oakland in exchange for the man they hope will add much-needed punch to their offence.

The Cardinals have suffered 17 one-run defeats this season, including seven in which they scored just one run or less. That should change with the addition of McGwire, one of the game's most prolific sluggers of all time.
McGwire is batting .284 with 81 RBI and is averaging one home run every 10.8 at-bats this season, his 11th full year in the majors.

McGwire helped the Athletics to four Western Division championships, three American League pennants and the 1989 World Series title and leaves Oakland as the all-time franchise leader in home runs with 363.
"I've had a great 11 years here," said McGwire, who thanked the Oakland fans in a farewell news conference.
McGwire's career home run ratio of one every 12.25 at-bats is second only to Babe Ruth's one per 11.76 at-bats. Over the last four seasons, McGwire's ratio is an astounding one per 9.27 at-bats.
Jason Giambi, who will move from the outfield to first base as McGwire's replacement, said it was "probably the saddest day of my baseball career."
"You don't replace a player like that," he said. "He took me under his wing and taught me how to play the game."

Mathews, 27, could assume the closer's role for Oakland, which owns the worst record in the American League. He was 4-4 with no saves and 2.15 ERA in 40 relief appearances for the Cardinals this year.

"T.J. is the only one I'm familiar with," Athletics manager Art Howe said of his trio of new players. "I scouted him when I was with the Dodgers and he has an outstanding arm. I'm excited to get a pitcher of his calibre."
